source: NYISO real-time zonal LBMP & Moses South interface flow, Jan 2023 – Dec 2025
findings: Upstate: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$0.70/MWh on average) and lightest in Spring ($0.33/MWh).
Lower Hudson Valley: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$4.49/MWh on average) and lightest in Fall (−$0.38/MWh).
New York City: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$9.64/MWh on average) and lightest in Fall (−$1.00/MWh).
Long Island: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$10.81/MWh on average) and lightest in Fall (−$0.74/MWh).
In New York City, congestion peaks at 7–8 pm in July (−$12.06/MWh) and at 8–9 pm in January (−$39.44/MWh).
Weekdays are more congested than weekends in 8 of 11 zones. The biggest gap is J · New York City: −$3.97/MWh on weekdays vs −$2.99/MWh on weekends.
Of New York City's 10 worst days, 9 were in Winter and 8 fell on weekdays. The worst was 2024-01-17 (Wednesday) at −$155.52/MWh.
Worst single months: K · Long Island in Jan 2024 (−$16.33/MWh); J · New York City in Jan 2024 (−$19.08/MWh); F · Capital in Jan 2024 (−$9.76/MWh).
cannot_conclude: Seeing congestion peak in a season or hour does not tell us why; weather, demand, outages and fuel prices all change at the same time.
Daily and monthly averages hide 5-minute spikes; the worst moments are much more extreme than these averages.
